unit_label: Module C unit 1 (courseware unit 17), part 3: special mention accounts, asset classification, income recognition, provisioning and the large exposures limits

facts.statement: Special mention accounts (SMAs) form an asset category between standard and sub-standard, introduced as an early warning mechanism so that a bank can act on incipient stress in a loan account before it slips into non-performing status. The courseware gives the categories for term loans by how long any principal, interest or other amount has been wholly or partly overdue: SMA-0 for 1 to 30 days, SMA-1 for 31 to 60 days and SMA-2 for 61 to 90 days. For revolving facilities such as cash credit there is no SMA-0; SMA-1 means the outstanding balance remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit or drawing power, whichever is lower, for 31 to 60 days and SMA-2 means the same for 61 to 90 days. Special mention accounts are not non-performing assets and so need no provisioning, but all irregularity and control reports and proposals should say whether the account is an SMA and which category.
facts.locator: S01 printed pp. 415-416 (PDF pp. 430-431), courseware account only; not found in RBI_IRACP_2025

facts.statement: A bank classifies a loan or advance as a non-performing asset (NPA) if any of the stated conditions holds, among them: interest or an instalment of principal remains overdue for more than 90 days on a term loan; an overdraft or cash credit account remains out of order; a working capital account has irregular drawings for a continuous period of 90 days; a bill purchased or discounted remains overdue for more than 90 days; regular or ad hoc credit limits have not been reviewed or renewed within 180 days of the due date or ad hoc sanction; the instalment of principal or interest remains overdue for two crop seasons for short duration crops or one crop season for long duration crops; a securitisation liquidity facility remains outstanding for more than 90 days; overdue receivables from a derivative contract stay unpaid for 90 days; and a credit card minimum amount due is not paid fully within 90 days of the payment due date. An NPA is an asset, including a leased asset, which has ceased to generate income for the bank.
facts.locator: RBI_IRACP_2025 paragraphs 5(6) and 42; courseware printed p. 417

facts.statement: A cash credit or overdraft account is out of order if any of the following holds: the outstanding balance remains continuously in excess of the sanctioned limit or drawing power for 90 days; the outstanding balance is below the limit or drawing power but there are no credits continuously for 90 days; or the outstanding is below the limit or drawing power but the credits are not enough to cover the interest debited during the previous 90 days. Asset classification is borrower-wise, not facility-wise: all facilities to a borrower and all investments in securities issued by the borrower are treated as NPA, not only the facility that has become irregular. Classification is based on the record of recovery, so temporary deficiencies, such as inadequate drawing power on the latest stock statement, a temporary excess over the limit, non-submission of stock statements or non-renewal of limits on the due date, do not by themselves make an account an NPA; the availability of security or the net worth of the borrower or guarantor is not taken into account in deciding whether an advance is an NPA (apart from the exception for the realisable value of security in paragraph 67).

A bank classifies an NPA into sub-standard, doubtful and loss assets according to the period it has remained non-performing and the realisability of the dues. A sub-standard asset is one that has remained an NPA for a period of up to and including twelve months; it has well defined credit weaknesses that jeopardise liquidation of the debt, with a distinct possibility of loss if deficiencies are not corrected. A doubtful asset is one that has remained in the sub-standard category for twelve months; it has all the weaknesses of a sub-standard asset with the added feature that collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently known facts, conditions and values, is highly questionable and improbable. A loss asset is one where loss has been identified by the bank, internal or external auditors or the Reserve Bank inspection, but the amount has not been written off wholly. Where there are potential threats to recovery, such as erosion in the value of security or the absence of security, and other factors such as fraud, the asset is classified straightaway as doubtful or loss. Erosion is significant when the realisable value of the security is less than fifty per cent of the value assessed by the bank or accepted by the Reserve Bank at the last inspection, and such NPAs may be classified straightaway as doubtful; if the realisable value of the security is less than ten per cent of the outstanding, the security is ignored and the asset is classified straightaway as a loss asset. An NPA may be upgraded to standard only when the entire arrears of interest and principal are paid by the borrower.

A bank may recognise income on the accrual basis only for facilities classified as standard; for facilities not classified as standard, including those guaranteed by Government, income is recognised on the actual receipt (cash) basis. If an advance, including bills purchased and discounted and Government guaranteed accounts, becomes an NPA, the entire interest accrued and credited to income in past periods is reversed if it is not realised; if a loan with a permitted interest moratorium turns into an NPA after the moratorium, the capitalised interest for the moratorium period need not be reversed. Interest realised on NPAs may be taken to income provided the credits towards interest are not out of fresh or additional facilities sanctioned to the same borrower. In the absence of a clear agreement on how recoveries in an NPA are appropriated (towards principal or interest), the bank must follow a uniform, consistent accounting principle. Interest on advances against term deposits, National Savings Certificates, Kisan Vikas Patras and life insurance policies may be taken to income on the due date if margin is adequate.
facts.locator: RBI_IRACP_2025 paragraphs 124-129, 135 and 136; courseware printed p. 416

facts.statement: A bank makes a general provision on standard assets, on the funded outstanding, on a global loan portfolio basis, at these rates: farm credit to agricultural activities, individual housing loans and Small and Micro Enterprises at 0.25 per cent; advances to the Commercial Real Estate (CRE) sector at 1.00 per cent; advances to the CRE - Residential Housing sector (CRE-RH) at 0.75 per cent; housing loans at teaser rates; restructured advances as stipulated in the resolution directions; and all other loans and advances at 0.40 per cent. Loans to Medium Enterprises attract 0.40 per cent. Standard asset provisions are not counted for arriving at net NPAs and are not netted from gross advances but shown separately as contingent provisions against standard assets. A bank estimates the risk of the unhedged foreign currency position of borrowers and makes incremental provision above the standard asset provision when likely loss / EBID exceeds 15 per cent, from 20 basis points (more than 15 and up to 30 per cent) to 80 basis points (more than 75 per cent).

The provisions on NPAs are: for sub-standard assets, a general provision of 15 per cent of the total outstanding, made without any allowance for ECGC cover and securities available; unsecured exposures (where the realisable value of the security is not more than ten per cent of the outstanding ab initio) identified as sub-standard attract an additional 10 per cent, so a total of 25 per cent; infrastructure loan accounts classified as sub-standard attract 20 per cent where the bank has a mechanism to escrow the cash flows and a clear legal first claim on them; for doubtful assets, 100 per cent of the extent to which the advance is not covered by the realisable value of the security to which the bank has valid recourse (estimated on a realistic basis) and, on the secured portion, 25 per cent if the asset has been doubtful for up to one year, 40 per cent for one to three years and 100 per cent for more than three years; for loss assets, which should be written off, 100 per cent of the outstanding if they are allowed to remain in the books. For leased assets the rates apply to the net investment in the lease and the unrealised portion of finance income net of the finance charge component. Security means tangible security properly charged to the bank and does not include guarantees, comfort letters and similar intangible security.

For existing loans to companies with a director (other than a nominee director of a government or financial institution brought on at the time of distress) whose name appears more than once in the list of wilful defaulters, the provision on standard accounts is five per cent, and if such an account is classified as an NPA it attracts accelerated provisioning at higher rates than the regular rates.

Under the Large Exposures Framework in the Concentration Risk Management Directions, a large exposure is an exposure to a counterparty or a group of connected counterparties that is equal to or above 10 per cent of the bank's eligible capital base. The eligible capital base is the effective amount of Tier 1 capital as per the last audited balance sheet. The sum of all exposure values of a bank to a single counterparty shall not exceed 20 per cent of the eligible capital base at all times; in exceptional cases the Board may allow an additional 5 per cent, under a Board-approved policy. The sum of exposures to a group of connected counterparties shall not exceed 25 per cent of the eligible capital base at all times. A breach of these limits must be under exceptional conditions beyond the bank's control, reported to the RBI immediately and rapidly rectified. Interbank exposures (other than intra-day) are subject to the large exposure limit of 25 per cent of Tier 1 capital, and a bank's exposure to a single NBFC, other than a gold loan company, is restricted to 20 per cent of its eligible capital base.
facts.locator: RBI_CONC_2025 paragraphs 4(6) and the definition of eligible capital base, 15, 16, 18, 62 and 79

facts.statement: Counterparties are a group of connected counterparties if at least one of two criteria is met: a control relationship, where one counterparty directly or indirectly controls the other or all are controlled by a third party, or economic interdependence, where the financial difficulty of one would probably cause difficulty for another. Economic interdependence is considered at a minimum where 50 per cent or more of one counterparty's gross receipts or gross expenditures on an annual basis comes from transactions with the other; where one has fully or partly guaranteed the exposure of the other, or is liable by other means, and the exposure is so significant that the guarantor is likely to default if a claim occurs; or where a significant part of one counterparty's output is sold to another that cannot easily be replaced by other customers. For investments in funds and securitisation structures a bank looks through to underlying assets whose exposure is 0.25 per cent or more of its eligible capital base, and may assign smaller exposures to the structure itself; if it cannot identify the underlying assets and its total exposure is 0.25 per cent or more, the amount is assigned to an unknown client. The Directions record the deletion with effect from 1 January 2026 of the chapter on enhancing credit supply to large borrowers through the market mechanism.
facts.locator: RBI_CONC_2025 paragraphs 20, 25, 63-66 and the deletion note on Chapter IV

payload.title: Special mention accounts: early warning before an NPA
payload.core_explanation_md:
RBI created a **special mention account (SMA)** class that sits **between standard and sub-standard** assets. The aim is **early identification of stress** so the bank can act (including rehabilitation or restructuring) before the account becomes an NPA.

| Category | Term loans: amount overdue (principal, interest or any other amount) | Revolving facilities such as cash credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **SMA-0** | **1 to 30 days** | **None**: this category does not exist |
| **SMA-1** | **31 to 60 days** | Balance **continuously above the limit or drawing power** (whichever is lower) for **31 to 60 days** |
| **SMA-2** | **61 to 90 days** | The same excess for **61 to 90 days** |

An SMA is **not an NPA**, so **no provision** is needed for it, but irregularity and control reports must **state whether the account is an SMA and which category**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md:
After 90 days the NPA tests in the next card apply, so SMA-2 is the last warning stage.

*Source note:* the bands follow paragraph 15 of the RBI Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, which sets SMA-0 for non-revolving loans only and SMA-1 and SMA-2 for revolving facilities.

self_check.prompt_text: A term loan instalment has been overdue for 45 days. Which SMA category is it?

payload.title: When an account becomes an NPA
payload.core_explanation_md:
An **NPA** is an asset (including a leased asset) that has **ceased to generate income** for the bank. A bank must classify an advance as NPA if **any** of these holds:

| Facility | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| **Term loan** | Interest or instalment overdue **more than 90 days** |
| **OD / CC** | Account stays **out of order** |
| **Working capital** | **Irregular drawings** for a continuous **90 days** |
| **Bills purchased / discounted** | Overdue **more than 90 days** |
| **Any limit** | Regular or ad hoc limit **not reviewed or renewed within 180 days** of the due date or ad hoc sanction |
| **Agriculture** | Overdue for **two crop seasons** (short duration crops) or **one crop season** (long duration crops) |
| **Securitisation liquidity facility** | Outstanding more than **90 days** |
| **Derivatives** | Overdue positive mark-to-market receivable unpaid for **90 days** |
| **Credit card** | Minimum amount due not paid in full within **90 days** of the due date |
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Remember "90 days" as the common clock, and 180 days for unreviewed limits.

self_check.prompt_text: Which facility has a 180-day test rather than a 90-day test?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A credit limit not reviewed or renewed within 180 days of the due date or ad hoc sanction.

payload.title: Out of order, borrower-wise classification and temporary deficiencies
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Out of order** (cash credit or overdraft): the account is out of order if **any** of these holds:

1. the balance stays **above the limit or drawing power for 90 days**;
2. the balance is within the limit but there are **no credits for 90 days**;
3. the balance is within the limit but **credits do not cover the interest debited in the previous 90 days**.

**Borrower-wise, not facility-wise:** when one facility turns NPA, **all facilities** to that borrower (and the bank's investments in the borrower's securities) are treated as NPA.

**Record of recovery decides.** Temporary deficiencies do **not** by themselves make an NPA: inadequate drawing power on the latest stock statement, a temporary excess over the limit, stock statements not submitted, or limits not renewed on the due date.

The **availability of security** or the **net worth** of the borrower or guarantor is **not** a reason to avoid NPA classification.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: There is one exception to the security rule, covered in the sub-standard, doubtful and loss card: where there is a potential threat to recovery from the value of security, the account can be classified doubtful or loss at once.

self_check.prompt_text: One of a borrower's three facilities has become an NPA. How are the other two classified?
self_check.expected_takeaway: As NPA too, because classification is borrower-wise.

payload.title: Sub-standard, doubtful and loss assets
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Category | Defining test | Nature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Sub-standard** | NPA for **up to and including 12 months** | **Well defined credit weaknesses**; distinct possibility of loss if not corrected |
| **Doubtful** | Remained sub-standard for **12 months** | All sub-standard weaknesses **plus** full recovery is **highly questionable and improbable** |
| **Loss** | **Loss identified** by the bank, auditors or RBI inspection, **not yet written off wholly** | Loss assets should be **written off** |

**Straight to doubtful or loss.** Where recovery is under threat from security or fraud:

- realisable value of security **less than 50 per cent** of the value assessed at the last valuation or inspection: the NPA **may be classified doubtful** straight away;
- realisable value **less than 10 per cent of the outstanding**: security is ignored and the asset is classified **loss** straight away.

**Upgrade:** an NPA goes back to standard only when the **whole arrears of interest and principal** are paid.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Time moves an asset from sub-standard to doubtful; a collapse in security value can move it faster.

self_check.prompt_text: After how long in the sub-standard category does an asset become doubtful?

payload.title: Recognising income on standard assets and on NPAs
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Account | Basis |
| --- | --- |
| **Standard** | **Accrual** basis |
| **Not standard** (including Government guaranteed) | **Actual receipt (cash)** basis |

**On becoming an NPA:** the interest already **accrued and credited to income** in past periods is **reversed** if not realised (including for bills and Government guaranteed accounts). Exception: capitalised interest for a **permitted moratorium period** need not be reversed.

**Interest actually recovered** in an NPA may be taken to income, **provided** the credit is **not out of fresh or additional facilities** granted to the same borrower (that would be evergreening).

**Appropriation:** without a clear agreement, the bank applies a **uniform and consistent** accounting principle to split recoveries between principal and interest.

**Exception:** interest on advances against **term deposits, NSCs, KVPs and life insurance policies** can be taken to income **on the due date** if the margin is adequate.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Why this matters: profit must not be inflated by interest that is only a book entry.

self_check.prompt_text: May interest on an NPA be taken to income if it was paid from a fresh loan to the same borrower?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: only interest realised not out of fresh or additional facilities may be taken to income.

payload.title: Provisioning on standard assets
payload.core_explanation_md:
A bank makes a **general provision** on the **funded outstanding** of standard assets, on a **global loan portfolio basis**:

| Advances | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Farm credit to agricultural activities, **individual housing loans** and **Small and Micro Enterprises** | **0.25 per cent** |
| **Commercial real estate (CRE)** | **1.00 per cent** |
| **CRE - residential housing (CRE-RH)** | **0.75 per cent** |
| All other loans and advances (including **Medium Enterprises**) | **0.40 per cent** |

(Teaser rate housing loans and restructured advances have their own stipulated treatment.)

- These provisions are **not** used to arrive at **net NPAs**.
- They are **not netted** from gross advances; they are shown as **contingent provisions against standard assets** under other liabilities and provisions.
- Borrowers with **unhedged foreign currency exposure** may need **extra** provision of **20 to 80 basis points** on the bank's total exposure to them, depending on likely loss as a share of EBID.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Note the courseware lists small and micro enterprises and farm credit at 0.25 per cent; the Directions also place individual housing loans in this group.

self_check.prompt_text: What standard asset provision applies to a loan to a Medium Enterprise?

payload.title: Provisioning on NPAs
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Category | Provision |
| --- | --- |
| **Sub-standard** | **15 per cent** of total outstanding (no allowance for ECGC cover or securities) |
| Sub-standard, **unsecured** (security realisable value not more than 10 per cent of the outstanding ab initio) | **25 per cent** (15 + 10 extra) |
| Sub-standard **infrastructure** loans with escrow of cash flows and a first claim | **20 per cent** |
| **Doubtful** | **100 per cent** of the part **not covered by the realisable value of security**, plus on the **secured portion**: **25 per cent** (up to 1 year), **40 per cent** (1 to 3 years), **100 per cent** (over 3 years) |
| **Loss** | **Write off**; if kept in the books, **100 per cent** |

"Security" means **tangible** security properly charged to the bank; **guarantees, comfort letters** and similar are **not** security for this purpose. For **leased assets** the same rates apply to the net investment in the lease plus the unrealised finance income, net of the finance charge component.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Remember the pattern: unsecured portions go to 100 per cent once the asset is doubtful, secured portions step up with time.

self_check.prompt_text: What is the provision on the secured portion of a doubtful asset that has been doubtful for two years?

payload.expanded_explanation_md: The Directions give the accelerated rates in a table that this course does not reproduce.

self_check.prompt_text: What provision applies to a standard account of a company whose director is on the wilful defaulter list more than once?

payload.title: Provision for a doubtful asset with partly covered security
payload.core_explanation_md: A loan of Rs 80 lakh has been a doubtful asset for 18 months. The realisable value of the tangible security properly charged to the bank is Rs 50 lakh. Find the provision required.

worked_steps.description: Secured portion is the part covered by realisable value of security.
Unsecured portion = outstanding minus secured portion; provision 100 per cent.
Doubtful for 18 months falls in the one-to-three-year band: 40 per cent on the secured portion.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Total provision Rs 50 lakh, which is 62.5 per cent of the outstanding

self_check.prompt_text: If the same loan had been doubtful for six months, what would the provision be?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Rs 42.5 lakh: Rs 30 lakh for the unsecured part plus 25 per cent of Rs 50 lakh = Rs 12.5 lakh.

payload.title: The Large Exposures Framework: limits
payload.core_explanation_md:
The **eligible capital base** is the bank's **Tier 1 capital** from the **last audited balance sheet**.

| Exposure to | Limit (of eligible capital base) |
| --- | --- |
| A **single counterparty** | **20 per cent** at all times; the **Board** may allow **5 per cent more** in exceptional cases under an approved policy |
| A **group of connected counterparties** | **25 per cent** at all times |
| Interbank (not intra-day) | **25 per cent** of Tier 1 capital |
| A single **NBFC** (not a gold loan company) | **20 per cent** |

A **large exposure** is one that is **10 per cent or more** of the eligible capital base (to a counterparty or a connected group). A **breach** must come from **exceptional conditions beyond the bank's control**, be **reported to RBI immediately** and **rectified quickly**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The limits apply to all exposures taken together, not facility by facility.

self_check.prompt_text: Up to what percentage of its eligible capital base may a bank lend to one counterparty, if its Board allows the extra in exceptional cases?
self_check.expected_takeaway: 25 per cent (20 per cent plus an additional 5 per cent).

payload.title: Connected counterparties and look-through
payload.core_explanation_md:
Counterparties are a **group of connected counterparties** if **either** test is met:

- **Control:** one controls the other (directly or indirectly), or a **third party controls all**;
- **Economic interdependence:** trouble in one would likely cause trouble in another. Minimum tests include: **50 per cent or more** of one party's **gross receipts or expenditure** is from the other; one has **guaranteed** the other's exposure so heavily that a claim would likely make the guarantor default; or a large part of one party's **output** is sold to another it **cannot easily replace**.

**Funds and securitisation structures:** the bank **looks through** to underlying assets whose share is **0.25 per cent or more** of its eligible capital base. Smaller ones can be assigned to the **structure itself**. If the bank **cannot identify** the underlying assets and its total exposure is **0.25 per cent or more**, the amount goes to an **unknown client**.

**Out of date:** the older **large borrower market mechanism** chapter was **deleted from 1 January 2026**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Two companies with no shareholding link can still be one group if one depends on the other for half its sales.

self_check.prompt_text: Company A sells 60 per cent of its output revenue to Company B. Could they be connected counterparties?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes, by economic interdependence: 50 per cent or more of one party's gross receipts comes from the other.

payload.title: Computing the exposure limits for a bank
payload.core_explanation_md: A bank has Tier 1 capital of Rs 5,000 crore in its last audited balance sheet. Find the single counterparty limit, the limit if the Board allows the additional amount, the group limit and the large exposure threshold.

worked_steps.description: Eligible capital base is Tier 1 capital.
With Board approval for the extra 5 per cent.
Group of connected counterparties: 25 per cent.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Single counterparty Rs 1,000 crore (Rs 1,250 crore with the Board allowance), group Rs 1,250 crore, large exposure threshold Rs 500 crore

self_check.prompt_text: An exposure of Rs 600 crore to one counterparty: is it a large exposure, and is it within the limit?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Yes it is a large exposure (above Rs 500 crore), and it is within the Rs 1,000 crore limit.

unresolved: Special mention accounts (SMA-0, SMA-1, SMA-2): the categories are taught from the courseware (printed pp. 415-416) and marked needs_review. The SMA bands are set in paragraph 15 of the RBI Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 (RBI_RSA_2025); the Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions do not contain them.

The 2025 Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions (RBI/DOR/2025-26/164) were read for paragraphs 5, 42-46, 63-71, 80-96, 118 and 124-136. The copy is marked as updated on 1 October 2026 and includes amendments effective 1 July 2026 (after the 30 June 2026 cut-off): the deletion of item (6) of paragraph 80 and new paragraphs 84A to 84D on additional specific provision for implemented resolution plans. These amendments are NOT taught.

The courseware lists the 0.25 per cent standard asset rate for farm credit and for small and micro enterprises; the 2025 Directions apply it to farm credit to agricultural activities, individual housing loans and Small and Micro Enterprises (SMEs). The Directions are followed.

The courseware states that no provision is needed for the guaranteed portion of ECGC, CGTMSE or credit guaranteed accounts that turn non-performing; paragraph 85 of the Directions states that the 15 per cent provision on substandard assets is made without allowance for ECGC cover. This is unresolved and is NOT taught. The courseware's account of the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (printed pp. 418-419: ceilings, guarantee coverage table) was not checked against a primary source and is NOT taught.

The courseware's accelerated provisioning table (printed p. 418) is in the Directions only under paragraph 118 (wilful defaulters); its columns were garbled in extraction and the rates are NOT taught, only the 5 per cent rate for standard accounts and the fact that accelerated provisioning applies on NPA classification.

The Concentration Risk Management Directions (RBI/DOR/2025-26/158) were read for the Large Exposures Framework paragraphs 4, 15, 16, 18, 20, 25, 62 and 64-66 and 79 only. They record the deletion, with effect from 1 January 2026, of the Chapter on enhancing credit supply to large borrowers through the market mechanism. The courseware's account of the large borrower, Specified Borrower and loan system framework is therefore out of date and is NOT taught. Other exposure norms (sectoral limits, capital market and real estate exposure, which the copy shows as amended from 1 October 2026) were not read.
Printed pp. 419 onward were not taught from: the CGTMSE material on pp. 418-419 is held back, and pp. 420 to 421 (transfer of accounts, fair practices, summary) and the later pages are not yet used.
